div.l: Ye ben to me wolcom / Ryght hertely Prologꝰus
For bi my trouth / if that I shal na lye
I saw nat this yeer / such a companye
Attones in this herberwe / as is nowe
Fayn wolde I doon yow myrthe / wyst I howe
And of a myrth / I am ryht nowe by thoht
To doon you ese / and it shall cost you nowht
Ye gon to Cantirbury / god you spede
The blisful martir / quyte you your mede
And wel I wot / as ye goon by the wey
Ye shapen you / to Iapen and to pley
For truly comford / ne myrthe is it noon
To ryden by the wey / Doomb as the ston
And therfor wol I make / you disport
As I seid erst / and do you som comfort
And if you lyketh al / bi on assent
For to stondyn / as my Iugement
And for to werkyn / as I shall yo seye
To morwyn / whan ye ryden bi the weye
Nowe bi my fadir sowle / that is deede
But ye be mery / y yeve you myn heede
Holdeth vp your handys / wythoutēn more speche
Owr conseil was nat long / for to seche
Vs thouht it was nat worth / to make it wys
And graunted him / wythouten more avys
And bad him sey / his wordys all him leste
Lordynges ꝙquod he / nowe herkeneth for the beste
But takyth it nat / I pray you in disdeyn
This is the poynt / to speke shor and pleyn
That eche of you / / to short wᵗith your wey
In this vyage / shal telle talys twey
To Cantirbury . warde / I mene it so
And homwarde / he shall tellyn othir too /
Of aventurs / that somtyme haue byfall
And whiche of you / bereth him best of all
